title: Scalar realization preserves resolving pairs and their localization tensors
statement: For a finite commutative ring R and scheme T, the scalar realization carries the flat-term K-flat complexes of [lem-sf-finite-scalar-tensor-complex] into intrinsic flat-term K-flat complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Restriction from functors on pairs of fixed derived objects to pairs in this resolving class is fully faithful. The inverse native localization tensorator gives the fixed derived tensor representative isomorphism on these pairs.

proof.text: An exact tensor equivalence preserves term flatness by conjugating tensor-right with its inverse, and preserves K-flatness by lifting every acyclic test complex through the inverse equivalence and using the total tensor isomorphism.
Use flat-term K-flat resolutions and the homotopy quotient to show fully faithful restriction to pairs of these representatives.

In abstract monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories, the homotopy localization tensor counit is invertible on a K-flat right input. The cochain quotient is strong monoidal, so its composite tensorator is invertible. Assemble these tensorators naturally on an arbitrary specified K-flat class and invert the resulting natural transformation. Specialize this generic construction to the fixed flat-term K-flat class; this avoids repeatedly unfolding the concrete monoidal instances.
